headline: Cave Permits and Dark Sky Preservation
reservation: Entry requires a standard National Monument fee or pass; however, all cave exploration requires a free permit obtained in person at the Visitor Center. Permits are subject to a screening for White-Nose Syndrome to protect bats. Camping at Lava Flow is first-come, first-served, so check official status for site availability before arriving with an RV.

days.title: Craters and Cones

stops.name: Inferno Cone
stops.detail: Climb the steep cinder slope for a panoramic view of the Great Rift and the distant Pioneer Mountains.

stops.name: Spatter Cones
stops.detail: Walk the short, paved path to look down into the throat of these miniature volcanic vents.

days.driving: Under 30 minutes on the 7-mile Loop Road; conditions vary with wind
days.note: Black lava rock absorbs heat; midday temperatures on the cinder cones can be extreme.

days.title: Subterranean Lava Tubes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Indian Tunnel
stops.detail: Explore the largest and most accessible lava tube in the park, featuring collapsed roof sections for natural light.

stops.name: Dewdrop Cave
stops.detail: Visit Dewdrop Cave only when open, with the required free cave permit; check current conditions at the visitor center.

days.driving: Local transfers on the Loop Road; allow 15 minutes
days.note: Bring a dedicated headlamp; smartphone flashlights are insufficient for cave safety.

days.title: High Desert Ecology
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Loop Road Entrance

stops.name: Devil’s Orchard
stops.detail: Take the accessible 0.5-mile boardwalk through 'islands' of lava and sagebrush to see hardy limber pines.

stops.name: North Crater Flow Trail
stops.detail: Walk among jagged 'a'a lava formations and pressure ridges to see the youngest flows in the monument.

days.driving: Local transfers; total Loop Road circuit takes about 45 minutes without stops
days.note: Stay on marked trails to protect the fragile cinder crust which takes decades to recover from footprints.

intel.title: Cave Area Capacity
intel.text: The parking lot for the Cave Trail is small and often reaches capacity by 11 AM. Plan to visit the lava tubes early in the morning for easier access.

intel.title: Desert Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is mostly unavailable once you leave the Highway 20 corridor near Arco. The visitor center offers the last reliable point for digital communication.

intel.title: High Desert Fueling
intel.text: There is no fuel available within the National Monument. Arco is the closest reliable station to the east; Carey is the closest to the west.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Loops
intel.text: The 7-mile Loop Road is closed to motorized vehicles in winter, typically from late November through April, when it is reserved for skiing.

intel.title: Cave Gear Screening
intel.text: To prevent bat disease, you cannot bring any item into the caves that has ever been in another cave. Expect a verbal screening at the Visitor Center before your permit is issued.

plan.arrival: Pick up your car at Friedman Memorial (SUN) and drive 65 minutes east. Stop in Arco for a meal and groceries before entering the monument.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is ideal for the Loop Road; RVs are permitted but will find parking in the Cave Area and at Spatter Cones very tight.
plan.goldenHour: Inferno Cone provides the best vantage for sunset, though high desert winds often intensify as the sun goes down.
